template.name: post_incident_review
template.description: Blameless post-incident review for a production outage. Reconstruct the timeline, identify root cause vs triggers and contributing factors, agree on follow-ups with owners, and capture lessons for systemic improvement.

sections.label: Incident timeline
sections.description: Chronological sequence of key events with timestamps and sources (alerts, deploys, user reports, mitigations); stick to factual what/when without interpretation.

sections.label: Impact and scope
sections.description: Who/what was affected and how badly: services/regions, user segments, duration, error rates, data loss, SLO/SLA breaches, and business/customer impact.

sections.label: Detection and response
sections.description: How the issue was detected, escalated, communicated, and mitigated; alert coverage and response process effectiveness—summarize process quality rather than restating timeline events.

sections.label: Root cause
sections.description: Agreed systemic cause statement describing the underlying defect or gap that made the incident possible; avoid blaming individuals.

sections.label: Triggers
sections.description: Immediate precipitating event(s) that activated the latent issue (e.g., specific deploy, config change, traffic spike, dependency outage).

sections.label: Contributing factors
sections.description: Non-trigger conditions that increased likelihood or impact: technical debt, test gaps, capacity limits, runbook quality, tooling/organizational/process issues.

sections.label: Follow-up actions
sections.description: Concrete corrective or preventive tasks with owner, due date, and acceptance criteria; include both technical fixes and process improvements.

sections.label: Lessons learned
sections.description: Generalizable insights (what helped, what to change) that inform future design, operations, and on-call practice; avoid duplicating items already tracked as actions.

sections.label: Other
sections.description: Anything material that doesn't fit a declared section. Prefer declared sections; use this only when nothing else fits.

phases.label: Rapport and scope
phases.goal: Set a blameless tone, confirm purpose, agenda, timebox, and who is present.

phases.label: Reconstruct the incident
phases.goal: Build a shared factual timeline and quantify impact; capture how detection and response unfolded.

phases.label: Analyze causes
phases.goal: Differentiate root cause from immediate triggers and broader contributing factors; align on the causal chain.

phases.label: Actions and learning
phases.goal: Translate findings into concrete follow-ups with owners and dates; capture key lessons to improve systems and process.

phases.label: Wrap
phases.goal: Read back decisions, owners, and deadlines; confirm publication plan and next check-in.

issues.description: Wrap phase has no sections in focus; read-back of owners/dates often benefits from explicitly re-surfacing follow_up_actions for confirmation.
issues.suggested_fix: Add "follow_up_actions" to wrap.sections_in_focus to guide a concise read-back and confirmation.

issues.description: Impact details and core incident metadata (incident ID, severity, start/end times, links) may get split between timeline and impact_and_scope.
issues.suggested_fix: Optionally add a small "incident_metadata" section (repeated=false) for ID/severity/timestamps/links to keep timeline purely event-based and impact purely effects-based.

critique.rationale: The template closely matches the user’s intent: clear timeline reconstruction, explicit separation of root cause vs triggers vs contributing factors, concrete follow-ups with owners, and lessons learned, all with a blameless/systemic framing. Structure is solid with 8 substantive sections, 5 well-paced phases totaling 1.0, and concrete, distinguishable section descriptions.
